# Creating and Configuring Forms and Flow Form Process Files

## Field of the Disclosure

This disclosure relates to the creation and configuration of forms, as well as the management of flow form process files, within a data storage system. The described techniques provide flexible mechanisms for defining, customizing, and deploying forms while streamlining the underlying data processing workflows.

## Automated Discovery of Available Actions

One notable feature of the system is its ability to auto-discover some or all of the available actions that can be performed on a particular type of record. Rather than requiring these actions to be manually defined or hard-coded, the system derives them from a set of stored form flow process files. By analyzing these process files, the system can automatically identify the operations applicable to a given record type, thereby reducing configuration overhead and ensuring that the available actions remain consistent with the underlying process definitions.

## Establishing a Configurable Form

The system supports the establishment of configurable forms through a structured process. Establishing such a form involves receiving a form file that includes both an acceptability filter and at least one non-mandatory form item. Each non-mandatory form item can be selectively toggled on or off, allowing the form to be tailored to specific requirements without necessitating changes to its fundamental structure. This approach provides significant flexibility, enabling a single form definition to accommodate a variety of use cases.

## Role of the Applicability Filter

Central to the configurable form is the applicability filter, which governs how and when non-mandatory form items are presented. Specifically, the applicability filter determines the circumstances under which non-mandatory form items are applied and displayed alongside mandatory items on a graphical user interface. In this way, the filter ensures that only the relevant optional items appear in a given context, while mandatory items are consistently presented. This selective display improves usability and helps guide the user through the form in a manner appropriate to the situation.

## Code-Free Data Source Selection

The disclosure further describes a search list that simplifies the process of specifying data sources. Through this search list, a user can nominate which data source should be used without requiring any code. By eliminating the need for manual programming, the search list lowers the technical barrier to configuration and enables users to select and change data sources quickly and intuitively.

## Summary

Taken together, these features—automated action discovery, configurable forms with toggleable non-mandatory items, an applicability filter governing item display, and a code-free data source search list—provide a comprehensive and flexible framework for creating and configuring forms and flow form process files within a data storage system.

# Configurable Form and Flow Form Process File Creation System

## Overview

This disclosure addresses the creation and configuration of forms and flow form process files through an innovative approach that leverages acceptability filters and dynamically controllable form items. The system is designed to simplify and streamline the process of building and customizing forms, particularly for users who may not possess programming expertise.

## Core Functionality

At the heart of this disclosure is the use of an acceptability filter working in conjunction with non-mandatory form items. These non-mandatory items can be toggled on or off based on established circumstances or predefined conditions. This conditional behavior allows forms to adapt dynamically to varying situations, presenting only the relevant fields and options to the user based on the context in which the form is being used.

In addition to this conditional item management, the system enables the auto-discovery of available actions that can be performed on various record types. Rather than requiring manual specification of possible operations, the system automatically identifies and surfaces the actions applicable to each record type. This auto-discovery capability reduces the burden on users configuring the forms and ensures that all valid actions are readily available.

## The Configurable Form File

The resulting configurable form file serves as the primary output of this system. When rendered, it displays both mandatory items—those required in all circumstances—and conditionally-applied non-mandatory items on a graphical user interface. This distinction ensures that users interacting with the form always encounter the essential fields while also being presented with additional fields only when appropriate to the established circumstances.

## Code-Free Data Source Selection

A key feature of the configurable form file is its inclusion of a code-free search list for nominating data sources. This functionality allows users to select and designate the data sources that will populate or interact with the form without needing to write any code. Through this search list, users can browse available data sources and make their selections through the graphical interface alone.

## Benefits

By combining conditional form items, acceptability filtering, auto-discovery of record actions, and code-free data source selection, this disclosure significantly streamlines the process of form customization. Users are empowered to create sophisticated, context-aware forms and flow form process files without requiring programming knowledge, thereby lowering the technical barrier to entry and accelerating the form-building workflow.

# Patent Abstract

**System and Method for Creating and Configuring Forms and Flow Form Process Files**

A system and method for creating and configuring electronic forms and flow form process files is disclosed. The system enables users to design forms and define multi-step process flows through a configuration interface. The system includes an auto-discovery module that automatically identifies and surfaces available actions associated with one or more record types, thereby eliminating the need for manual specification of actions and reducing configuration errors. Upon selection of a record type, the auto-discovery module queries associated metadata to determine executable actions, which are presented to the user for inclusion in a form or flow process.

The system further employs applicability filters that govern the display and inclusion of optional form items. Each applicability filter defines one or more conditions evaluated against contextual data, record attributes, user attributes, or process state. When the conditions of an applicability filter are satisfied, corresponding optional form items are rendered or made available within the form or flow; otherwise, such items are suppressed. This conditional configuration allows forms and flow form process files to dynamically adapt to varying data contexts and user scenarios without requiring separate form definitions.

In embodiments, the flow form process files link a plurality of forms and actions into a sequenced workflow, wherein transitions between steps may be conditioned upon applicability filters and results of executed actions. The system thereby provides an efficient, error-reduced framework for generating context-aware forms and orchestrating record-based process flows.

# System and Method for Configurable Electronic Forms with Rule-Based Applicability and No-Code Data Source Configuration

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to electronic data collection systems, and more particularly to a configurable forms platform employing applicability filters, optionally-mandatory form elements, and no-code data source selection mechanisms.

## BACKGROUND

Conventional electronic forms systems require substantial programmatic intervention to define conditional field behavior, establish data bindings, and enforce completion requirements, thereby necessitating specialized development resources and impeding rapid form deployment by non-technical personnel.

## SUMMARY

Disclosed herein is a system comprising one or more processors and a non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed, cause the system to render a configurable electronic form comprising a plurality of form items, wherein said system implements applicability filters, non-mandatory item designations, and a no-code data source selection interface.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION

### Applicability Filters

**[0001]** In one embodiment, the system comprises an applicability filter subsystem configured to evaluate one or more conditional predicates against a set of contextual parameters, said contextual parameters including, but not limited to, user attributes, antecedent form item responses, temporal parameters, and external state values, whereby the visibility, enablement, or inclusion of one or more form items is dynamically determined.

**[0002]** The applicability filter may comprise a logical expression tree evaluable in real time responsive to state mutations within the form, wherein satisfaction of a predicate condition selectively triggers presentation of a dependent form item, and non-satisfaction thereof suppresses said dependent form item from a rendered output without removal from an underlying form definition schema.

**[0003]** In a further embodiment, said applicability filters are chainable and nestable, such that a first filter may be conditioned upon the evaluated result of a second filter, thereby defining a hierarchical dependency graph governing form item disposition.

### Non-Mandatory Form Items

**[0004]** The system further comprises a mandatory-designation subsystem wherein each form item is associated with a mandatoriness attribute selectably assignable between a mandatory state and a non-mandatory state, said non-mandatory state permitting submission of the form absent a populated value for the associated form item.

**[0005]** In a preferred embodiment, the mandatoriness attribute is itself conditionally determinable as a function of an applicability filter output, whereby a given form item may transition between mandatory and non-mandatory states responsive to satisfaction of one or more predicate conditions, thereby establishing conditional-requirement semantics.

**[0006]** The system may validate a submitted form instance against the aggregate mandatoriness attributes of its constituent form items, permitting submission upon satisfaction of all mandatory items while tolerating absence of values for items designated non-mandatory.

### No-Code Data Source Selection

**[0007]** The system additionally comprises a no-code data source selection interface configured to receive, via declarative user input and absent authored program code, a designation of one or more data sources from a plurality of available data sources, wherein each said data source is bindable to one or more form items for at least one of population, validation, and persistence of form item values.

**[0008]** In one embodiment, said available data sources comprise internal datastores, external application programming interfaces, database query endpoints, and static enumerated value sets, wherein the selection interface presents said available data sources in a graphical selection element and establishes a binding responsive to user selection therefrom.

**[0009]** The no-code data source selection interface may further expose configurable mapping parameters whereby fields of a selected data source are associated with corresponding form items through declarative correspondence definitions, said correspondence definitions being persisted within the form definition schema and evaluated at render time to effectuate data retrieval and binding.

**[0010]** In a further embodiment, the selection of a data source and the establishment of associated bindings are performed entirely through interaction with graphical interface elements, thereby obviating any requirement for authored source code and enabling configuration by non-technical operators.

### Integration

**[0011]** In a combined embodiment, the applicability filter subsystem, the mandatory-designation subsystem, and the no-code data source selection interface operate cooperatively, wherein an applicability filter predicate may reference a value retrieved from a no-code-configured data source, and wherein said value may further determine the mandatoriness state of a dependent form item, thereby yielding a unified, declaratively-configurable form behavior model.

## CLAIMS

**1.** A system for configurable electronic form generation, comprising: one or more processors; and memory storing instructions that, when executed, cause the system to: evaluate at least one applicability filter comprising a conditional predicate to selectively determine disposition of a form item; assign to said form item a selectable mandatoriness attribute; and receive, via a no-code selection interface, a designation binding said form item to a data source of a plurality of available data sources.

**2.** The system of claim 1, wherein the mandatoriness attribute is conditionally determined responsive to an output of the applicability filter.

**3.** The system of claim 1, wherein the applicability filter references a value retrieved from the data source bound via the no-code selection interface.

**4.** The system of claim 1, wherein the no-code selection interface establishes said binding responsive solely to graphical interface interaction and absent authored program code.

# Summary of the Disclosure

The following presents a simplified summary of the disclosure in order to provide a basic understanding of some aspects described herein. This summary is not an extensive overview and is not intended to identify key or critical elements or to delineate the scope of the claims. Its sole purpose is to present some concepts in a simplified form as a prelude to the more detailed description that is presented later.

## Overview

Disclosed herein are systems, methods, and computer-readable media for generating and managing configurable forms, orchestrating configurable flow-based form processes, and automatically discovering actions available for a particular type of record within a computing environment. The disclosed technology addresses limitations of conventional form systems, which typically require hard-coded form definitions, manually programmed process flows, and predetermined action sets that must be individually configured for each record type.

## Configurable Forms

In one aspect, the disclosure provides a system for defining configurable forms without requiring modification of underlying application source code. In some embodiments, a form definition is stored as structured metadata that specifies one or more form elements, including fields, controls, layout parameters, validation rules, and data bindings. A rendering engine interprets the metadata at runtime to generate a corresponding user interface. Because the form is defined by configurable metadata rather than compiled code, a form may be created, modified, versioned, or deprecated without redeployment of the underlying application.

In some embodiments, form elements are conditionally displayed, enabled, required, or validated based on rules evaluated against contextual data, user attributes, or values entered into other form elements. This permits a single form definition to adapt dynamically to different users, contexts, and data states.

## Configurable Flow Form Processes

In another aspect, the disclosure provides a system for defining and executing configurable flow form processes in which a plurality of forms, decision points, and actions are arranged into a sequence or graph that governs progression through a multi-step process. In some embodiments, a flow definition is stored as configurable metadata specifying a plurality of stages, transitions between stages, and conditions governing each transition.

In some embodiments, an orchestration engine evaluates the flow definition at runtime to determine which form to present at a given stage, to validate that conditions for advancing to a subsequent stage have been satisfied, and to route the process to a next stage based on data collected in one or more prior stages. Transitions may be conditioned on user input, record state, external system responses, or the outcome of executed actions. As a result, complex multi-step processes may be defined, altered, and maintained through configuration rather than custom programming.

## Auto-Discovery of Available Actions

In a further aspect, the disclosure provides for automatic discovery of actions available for a particular type of record. In some embodiments, the system identifies a record type associated with a record and queries one or more sources of action definitions to determine a set of candidate actions applicable to that record type. Action definitions may be associated with record types by metadata, by inheritance from a type hierarchy, by registration in an action registry, or by programmatic interfaces exposed by system components.

In some embodiments, the system further filters the set of candidate actions based on one or more of: the current state of the record, permissions or roles associated with a requesting user, contextual conditions, and applicability rules associated with each action. The resulting set of available actions may then be presented to a user, incorporated into a configurable form, or made available as transitions within a configurable flow form process. Because available actions are discovered dynamically at runtime, newly added actions become available for a record type automatically, without requiring reconfiguration of forms or flows that reference records of that type.

## Combined Operation and Advantages

In some embodiments, the foregoing aspects operate in combination. For example, a configurable flow form process may present a configurable form that includes controls corresponding to actions automatically discovered for a record of a particular type, and selection of such a control may drive a transition within the flow. This integration enables end-to-end configuration of data collection, process orchestration, and action execution through metadata rather than source code.

Among the potential advantages of certain embodiments are reduced development effort, decreased time to deploy new forms and processes, improved maintainability, greater consistency across an application, and the ability to extend functionality by adding new actions or record types without modifying existing forms or flows.

The foregoing summary is illustrative only and is not intended to be limiting. Additional aspects, features, and advantages of the disclosed subject matter will become apparent from the following detailed description, the accompanying drawings, and the claims. The described features may be combined in any suitable manner in one or more embodiments, and not all described features are required in any particular embodiment.

# Patent-Style Overview: System and Method for Conditional Display of Form Items Using Configurable Form Files and Flow Process Files

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to electronic data collection systems, and more particularly to a system and method for dynamically rendering graphical user interfaces wherein the display state and mandatory status of form items are conditionally controlled through the coordinated operation of configurable form definition files and flow form process files.

## BACKGROUND

Conventional electronic forms typically present a static arrangement of input fields, wherein the visibility and required status of each field is fixed at design time. Such systems suffer from several disadvantages, including presentation of irrelevant fields to users, inability to adapt field requirements based on prior user input, and the necessity of recompiling application code to modify form behavior. There exists a need for a system that separates form structure, conditional logic, and presentation, thereby enabling dynamic and configurable form behavior without modification of underlying application code.

## SUMMARY

The invention comprises three cooperating components:

1. **A configurable form file** that declaratively defines the structure, attributes, and default state of one or more form items.

2. **A flow form process file** that defines conditional logic, dependencies, and rules governing the display and mandatory status of said form items.

3. **A graphical user interface (GUI) rendering engine** that consumes the foregoing files and dynamically presents form items in accordance with evaluated conditions.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION

### 1. The Configurable Form File

The configurable form file comprises a structured data document (for example, encoded in a markup or object-notation format) containing a plurality of **form item definitions**. Each form item definition may include, without limitation:

- A **unique identifier** for referencing the item;
- A **display label** and associated help text;
- A **data type** (e.g., text, numeric, date, selection, boolean);
- A **default visibility attribute** (visible or hidden);
- A **default mandatory attribute** (mandatory or non-mandatory);
- **Validation constraints** (e.g., format, range, length); and
- **Grouping or hierarchical metadata** associating the item with parent sections or containers.

The configurable form file thereby establishes the *superset* of all possible form items and their baseline characteristics, independent of runtime conditions.

### 2. The Flow Form Process File

The flow form process file comprises a separate structured document defining the **conditional behavior** applied to the form items enumerated in the configurable form file. In one embodiment, the flow form process file comprises a plurality of **rule constructs**, each rule construct including:

- A **trigger condition** referencing one or more source form items and/or external context values (e.g., user role, prior submissions, system state);
- A **logical expression** evaluating said trigger condition (supporting operators such as equality, comparison, boolean conjunction and disjunction, and set membership); and
- One or more **resultant actions** specifying a change to a target form item's state, including:
  - Setting **visibility** (show/hide);
  - Setting **mandatory status** (require/optionalize);
  - Enabling or disabling input;
  - Populating or clearing values.

The flow form process file may further define **sequential flow paths** representing an ordered progression of form stages, wherein advancement from one stage to a subsequent stage is contingent upon satisfaction of specified conditions. This permits multi-step or branching workflows in which the visible and mandatory items at any given stage depend upon accumulated input.

### 3. The Graphical User Interface Rendering Engine

The GUI rendering engine is a software component configured to:

**(a)** Parse the configurable form file to instantiate an internal representation of the complete set of form items and their default states;

**(b)** Parse the flow form process file to construct an evaluable rule set and dependency graph mapping source items to affected target items;

**(c)** Render an initial interface presenting form items according to their default visibility and mandatory attributes as modified by any initial-state rules;

**(d)** Monitor user interaction events and context changes, and upon detecting a change to any monitored source item, **re-evaluate** the affected rule constructs;

**(e)** Apply resultant actions to update, in real time, the visibility and mandatory status of target form items within the displayed interface; and

**(f)** Enforce validation such that submission is permitted only when all currently-mandatory and currently-visible items satisfy their constraints.

---

## OPERATIONAL FLOW

In a representative operation:

1. The rendering engine loads the configurable form file and displays a subset of form items marked with a default visibility attribute of "visible."

2. A given form item is displayed with a **mandatory indicator** (for example, a visual marker) when its effective mandatory status resolves to true, and without such indicator when non-mandatory.

3. A user provides input to a source form item. For example, selecting a value in a "Filing Type" selection item satisfies a trigger condition defined in the flow form process file.

4. The rendering engine evaluates the associated logical expression and executes the resultant action—for instance, changing a dependent "Reason Description" item from hidden and non-mandatory to visible and mandatory.

5. The GUI is updated dynamically to reveal the newly-mandatory item and apply its mandatory indicator, without page reload and without modification of application source code.

6. Validation logic subsequently requires completion of the now-mandatory item prior to permitting progression along the flow path or final submission.

---

## ADVANTAGES

- **Separation of concerns:** Form structure (configurable form file), conditional logic (flow form process file), and presentation (GUI engine) are decoupled, enabling independent modification.

- **Configurability without recompilation:** Form behavior may be altered by editing declarative files rather than application code.

- **Dynamic relevance:** Only pertinent form items, and only appropriate mandatory requirements, are presented to the user based on real-time context.

- **Reusability:** A single rendering engine may operate upon arbitrary configurable form and flow process files to produce diverse form behaviors.

---

## CLAIMS (ILLUSTRATIVE)

**1.** A system for conditionally displaying form items, comprising: a processor; a memory storing a configurable form file defining a plurality of form items each having a default visibility attribute and a default mandatory attribute; a flow form process file defining a plurality of rule constructs each associating a trigger condition with a resultant action affecting the visibility or mandatory status of at least one of said form items; and a rendering engine executable by the processor to render a graphical user interface, evaluate said rule constructs responsive to user input, and dynamically modify the displayed visibility and mandatory status of said form items in accordance therewith.

**2.** The system of claim 1, wherein the flow form process file defines an ordered plurality of stages, advancement between which is contingent upon satisfaction of a condition evaluated against one or more of said form items.

**3.** The system of claim 1, wherein the rendering engine applies a visual mandatory indicator to a form item when its effective mandatory status resolves to true and permits form submission only upon satisfaction of validation constraints for all currently-visible mandatory form items.

---

*The foregoing description is illustrative of the principles of the invention and is not intended to limit the scope thereof. Numerous modifications and variations will be apparent to those skilled in the art without departing from the spirit of the invention.*
